conviction_note: Run-rate arithmetic (Q3 2025 $409M core less ~2.5-3 pts of P&C underlying deterioration, no Q2-style mass tort charge, benign industry cat quarter) points to roughly $1.27-1.36 core EPS against a disputed $1.16-1.23 bar, so the fundamental read is a modest beat (+5%); but the bar is unsettled, commercial pricing is visibly softening at every peer, and CNA sold its record Q3 2025 beat (-1.12%), so p_up sits only at 54 on an abs move of 2.8 (mean |reaction| 2.63% over 7 prints, no usable options); findings sum +0.70 vs scaled +0.22 because the reaction function on this name damps good numbers.
bar: Core EPS consensus is disputed across sources: $1.16 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/407866/cna-faces-a-lowered-bar-as-street-braces-for-a-23-third-quarter-earnings-decline), $1.19 on 2 estimates (ChartRow, https://chartrow.com/quote/cna/earnings), $1.20 (Earnings Whispers alt page), $1.23 with revenue $4.098B (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CNA/estimates, page 403 on fetch, snippet only). Year-ago Q3 2025 core EPS $1.50 ($409M). Working bar ~$1.20 (~$326M core on ~272M shares). No company guide exists beyond Q3 fixed-income NII of ~$575M (Q2 2026 remarks). Because the bar cannot be pinned to two exactly agreeing sources, every bar-dependent finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 3.82M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.0 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/cna, page dated 2026-10-23), up from 3.1M (2026-06-30, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cna/) and 2.86M (2026-05-29, 6.44 DTC, https://equibles.com/stocks/cna/short-interest). Loews owns ~90% of CNA, so the float is roughly 25-27M shares and 3.82M short is roughly 14-15% of float; Benzinga lists 13.4% short float (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CNA/sentiment). Crowded relative to float and rising into the print. Options: no usable chain (ATM spread 196% of mid, total OI 532, put/call OI 2.64), skew_25d null, so the option market makes no directional statement. Tape: +5.63% 20d run-up, +1.14% 5d, -11.5% from 52w high; Earnings Whispers says shares fell 11.1% since the August print before the recent recovery.

findings.finding: Run-rate build puts Q3 2026 core EPS near $1.27-1.36 against a $1.16-1.23 consensus: Q3 2025 core was $409M (P&C $456M, Corporate -$25M, L&G -$22M); applying the 2026 P&C underlying combined-ratio deterioration (+2.4 pts Q1, +2.5 pts Q2 to 94.2%, roughly -$60M after-tax a quarter), flat-ish LP income and Q3 fixed-income NII guided at ~$575M (vs $567M) gives ~$345-370M. Q3 carries no annual mass tort review (that was Q2's $77M after-tax Corporate charge; ex-charge Q2 was ~$401M, $1.47) and the A&EP review is Q4. The consensus implies ~$315-335M, a 20%+ YoY decline that needs either a heavy cat load or a fresh reserve charge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 record core $1.50 beat consensus (theinsurer.com headline 'CNA beats analysts' expectations') and the stock fell -1.12%; Q2 2026 core $1.19 with the mass tort charge: +2.13%; Q1 2026 core $0.83 with underlying CR +2.4 pts and $106M adverse PYD: -7.95%. Misses on underwriting are punished; beats are bought weakly or sold.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market held a ~$1.30 view, the published consensus would not sit 20-23% below the year-ago $1.50 with the mass tort review already behind it; with only 2-4 analysts the consensus may simply carry a hurricane-season cat load that did not arrive. But this is my arithmetic, not a document, and the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 segment numbers from a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21175/000002117525000093/q32025ex994earningsremarks.htm (2025-11-03). The consensus side comes from https://finviz.com/news/407866/cna-faces-a-lowered-bar-as-street-braces-for-a-23-third-quarter-earnings-decline. This build assumes cats near Q3 2025's 1.5 pts, so the cat finding below is the upside beyond that, not the same fact.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a light catastrophe quarter for US commercial insurers: Gallagher Re puts 9M26 global insured cat losses at $92bn, the lowest since 2019 and 29% below the 10-year average; Travelers' Q3 cats were $538M vs $695M expected; Hartford Business Insurance cats were $106M vs $389M a year earlier. CNA's cats are mostly US commercial SCS (Q2 2026 $60M, 2.3 pts; Q3 2025 $41M, 1.5 pts). Counter-evidence: Chubb North America Commercial cats rose to $237M from $72M, and US SCS was still at least $43bn through Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 cats of 3.6 pts ($97M) came with the -7.95% day; Q3 2025, with cats at 1.5 pts and a record quarter, was -1.12%. A light-cat beat has not been paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Peers printed between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-27, after CNA last spoke, and a thinly covered consensus may not have been refreshed. Partly priced: the +5.6% 20-day run-up overlaps the peer prints. If fully priced, the CNA consensus would have moved up toward the year-ago level; the sources show $1.16-1.23 instead.
findings.independence: Travelers cats vs expectations: https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/travelers-trv-q3-2026-usd-adj-eps-918-exp-739-revenue-124bln-exp-114bln ; Hartford BI cats: https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/10/27/890466.htm ; contrary Chubb NA commercial cats: https://actuary.info/insights/chubb-q3-2026-511m-releases-personal-lines-379m-commercial-14m . Industry proxy, not a CNA number.

findings.finding: Commercial pricing is softening at every peer that printed Q3 2026: Travelers' domestic BI rate ex-National Accounts was +0.9% vs +4.3% a year earlier, with renewal premium change 4.1% vs 7.1%; W. R. Berkley's rate increases roughly halved to ~4%; Chubb's NA commercial NPW fell 2.7% and Greenberg called the market 'more competitive'. CNA was already at flat P&C rate with renewal premium change slightly above 2% and International rate -5% in Q2, and its underlying loss ratio has risen ~2.5 pts YoY in each 2026 quarter. A further step down in CNA's rate or another rise in the underlying loss ratio lands on the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: underlying CR +2.4 pts, more conservative long-tail picks and adverse PYD: -7.95%. Q2 2026: underlying CR +2.5 pts but no P&C PYD: +2.13%. The underlying ratio alone has not been decisive; adverse development alongside it has been.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a sector theme: CNA fell about 11% after the August print. What is unpriced is the CNA-specific number. If the market expected CNA's rate to turn negative, the stock would not have recovered 5.6% over 20 days. Shrunk because about 14% of the float is short and a squeeze is a mechanism of its own.

findings.finding: Peers' Q3 2026 reserve reviews showed no fresh casualty strengthening: Travelers had $234M net favorable PYD despite a $295M asbestos add ($529M favorable ex-asbestos); Selective had zero casualty PYD vs -$40M a year earlier; Chubb NA commercial was +$14M favorable. CNA's P&C PYD was zero in Q2 2026 and Q3 2025 but -$106M in Q1 2026 (professional E&O), and adverse development is what accompanied CNA's -7.95% day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Adverse PYD quarter (Q1 2026): -7.95%. Zero-PYD quarters (Q2 2026, Q3 2025): +2.13% and -1.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer read-through that lowers the probability of the tail outcome rather than moving the mean. If the market feared a CNA charge, the stock would not have run up 5.6% into the print. Mostly priced; small.
findings.independence: Selective: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/breaking-news/selectives-casualty-reserves-stabilize-as-it-prices-out-weaker-commercial-accounts-594749.aspx . Proxy; CNA's own E&O issue was idiosyncratic. Note the Travelers asbestos add as a read-across risk for CNA's Q4 (not Q3) A&EP review.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest rose to 3.82M shares (2026-09-30, 5.0 days to cover) from 2.86M in May, roughly 14-15% of a ~26M-share float (Loews holds ~90%). Shorts are building into a print whose consensus already embeds a 20%+ YoY decline, so an in-line or better print has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CNA print is tied to short interest in the sources; the recent prints moved -1.12%, -1.40%, -7.95% and +2.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. It is filed because a crowded short on a ~26M-share float with ~355k average daily volume amplifies an upside surprise. If shorts had covered, the 2026-09-30 number would be falling, not rising.

findings.finding: Q3 carries the annual Life & Group reserve review (LTC and structured settlements). The last two were near neutral: -$7M after-tax in Q3 2025 (with $12M of favorable updates deferred to future periods) and -$5M in Q3 2024. A large LTC morbidity or cost-of-care change is the tail risk; the base case is under $0.03/share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (-$7M): -1.12% on the day, driven by P&C, not L&G. No recent L&G surprise has moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The review's timing is known and its history is small, so it is probably reflected. The deferred $12M favorable is a minor unpriced cushion.
findings.independence: CNA's Q2 2026 remarks confirm the Q3 timing of the L&G assumption updates: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021175/000002117526000043/q22026ex994earningsremarks.htm

findings.finding: Limited partnership and common stock income is likely lower than Q2's $131M (4.3%): the S&P 500 rose only ~2% in Q3 2026 and the equal-weight index fell 2.2%. This is near Q3 2025's $71M (2.5%), so neutral year-on-year and negative sequentially.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's higher LP income (+$31M YoY) came with a +2.13% day; no clean isolation.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts typically model LP income from public index returns, so it is mostly priced. Macro-to-company transmission, small.

baseline_tension: No usable option chain or skew, so the market's only directional statements are a +5.6% 20-day recovery and rising short interest (~14% of float); a modest-beat read agrees with the recovery and runs against the shorts, and the name's habit of selling good prints (record Q3 2025 beat: -1.12%) keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): consensus spans $1.16-1.23 across four aggregators, so the run-rate beat finding was capped from +0.8 to +0.5 and the light-cat finding from +0.6 to +0.4; print_vs_bar trimmed from +6 to +5

Rule 7 (crowded short against a negative): about 14% of float is short and rising, so the pricing-softening negative was shrunk from -0.6 to -0.4; the positioning finding was trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3 because shorts in a 90%-parent-owned name may be hedges
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): CNA sold its record Q3 2025 beat (-1.12%), so p_up went from 56 to 54 and the reaction stays small; abs_move unchanged at 2.8
Rule 5 (proxies filed small): the cat, pricing, reserve and LP findings are kept but labelled as proxies; no size change beyond the above
Rules 2, 4, 8 and 9: no one-off, financing or segment-only finding to resize; thin coverage noted, but no confirmed company-level unpriced number exists, so no upsizing
